accepted_examples.german: Hast du den neuen Boss getroffen?
accepted_examples.english: Have you met the new boss?
accepted_examples.note: Boss refers to a supervisor or person in charge.

accepted_examples.german: Es ist schön, Ihre Stimme wieder zu hören.
accepted_examples.english: It's great to hear your voice again.
accepted_examples.note: Stimme means a person's speaking voice here.

accepted_examples.german: Tom und Maria waren im Wagen sehr still.
accepted_examples.english: Tom and Mary were very quiet in the car.
accepted_examples.note: still describes people being quiet, matching the adjective sense.

accepted_examples.german: Warum setzen Sie sich nicht und entspannen sich?
accepted_examples.english: Why don't you sit down and relax?
accepted_examples.note: sich setzen means to sit down; the reflexive form is explicit.

accepted_examples.german: Sie waren zu müde, um zu kämpfen.
accepted_examples.english: They were too tired to fight.
accepted_examples.note: kämpfen is used as the plain infinitive meaning to fight.

accepted_examples.german: Was willst du für das ganze Zeug haben?
accepted_examples.english: How much do you want for all this stuff?
accepted_examples.note: Zeug is used colloquially for a collection of things or stuff.

accepted_examples.german: In diesem Sommer ist es unglaublich heiß.
accepted_examples.note: unglaublich intensifies the adjective heiß and means incredibly.

accepted_examples.german: Rücksichtsloses Fahren kann schnell zu einem Unfall führen.
accepted_examples.english: Reckless driving can easily lead to an accident.
accepted_examples.note: führen zu means to lead to or result in.

accepted_examples.german: Ich glaube nicht, dass Tom der Mörder ist.
accepted_examples.english: I don't believe Tom is the killer.
accepted_examples.note: Mörder names the person who committed a murder; the noun meaning is clear from context.

accepted_examples.german: Es gibt auf der Insel nur ein Geschäft.
accepted_examples.english: There's only one store on the island.
accepted_examples.note: Geschäft means a shop or store in this sentence.

accepted_examples.german: Sehe ich für dich wie ein Idiot aus?
accepted_examples.english: Do I look like an idiot to you?
accepted_examples.note: Idi(o)t is used as a noun referring to a person; this is colloquial and insulting language.
Verzeihung is the noun meaning forgiveness in the phrase um Verzeihung bitten.

accepted_examples.german: Du und ich, wir sind ein gutes Team.
accepted_examples.english: You and I make a good team.
accepted_examples.note: Team is used as a straightforward count noun.

accepted_examples.english: He was advanced to the rank of general.
accepted_examples.note: General refers to a military rank in this sentence.

accepted_examples.german: Ich hörte nur den Schluss von Toms Rede.
accepted_examples.english: I only heard the end of Tom's speech.
accepted_examples.note: Schluss means the end of a speech here.

accepted_examples.german: Du bist perfekt, so wie du bist.
accepted_examples.english: You're perfect the way you are.
accepted_examples.note: perfekt is a predicative adjective after bist.

accepted_examples.english: There is an urgent need for peace talks.
accepted_examples.note: nötig means necessary or needed; dringend contributes the urgent meaning.

plural_reviews.note: Stöcke is the standard plural for the stick sense; Stöcker is an attested regional alternative.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Use Stöcke as the standard form for wooden sticks. Stöcker is a regional variant.

plural_reviews.note: Nachbar is a weak masculine noun and forms the plural Nachbarn.

plural_reviews.value: Usually singular in the abstract 'best thing' sense
plural_reviews.note: Bestes is a substantivized superlative used chiefly as the singular das Beste. The forms Beste/Besten are declensional forms or refer to substantivized adjective uses, not a stable count plural for this abstract sense.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Usually singular when das Beste means the best thing. For several countable things, say die besten Dinge; die Besten commonly refers to the best people.

plural_reviews.note: Duden lists both Drehs and Drehe; the source does not mark either as wrong.
The regular plural of Pistole is Pistolen.
For this game-zone sense, the proper-noun-like game term takes the regular plural Leos.
Gentleman uses the borrowed plural Gentlemen.
Star meaning a starling has the German plural Stare; do not use Stars, which is the plural for a celebrity or celestial star sense.

plural_reviews.value: No regular plural in the mail-as-mass-noun sense
plural_reviews.note: Post meaning mail or post is normally a mass noun. Posten is a different sense such as a position or sentry, not the plural of mail.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Usually singular when Post means mail. Posten belongs to other senses such as a job/position or guard post.

plural_reviews.value: No regular plural in the abstract magic sense
plural_reviews.note: Duden gives only singular forms for abstract Magie; Langenscheidt labels the plural as absent.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Usually singular for magic as an abstract concept. Avoid Magien in general learner use.

plural_reviews.note: The technical line/alignment sense is countable and forms Fluchten; the abstract escape sense is normally singular.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Fluchten means alignments/lines in this technical sense. The abstract sense of escape is normally singular.

plural_reviews.note: Kohlen is the plural for separate pieces or kinds of coal; the material is commonly singular.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Kohle is usually singular as a mass noun; Kohlen can refer to pieces, supplies, or kinds of coal.
